newsitem.title: UK: Bridas opens office in Kabul, pursues gas project.
newsitem.headline: Bridas opens office in Kabul, pursues gas project.

text.p: Argentine energy independent Bridas has opened an office in Kabul, Afghanistan, to continue work on the construction of a natural gas pipeline from Turkmenistan through Afghanistan and Pakistan to India.

Sebastien Otero, manager of the Kabul office which is located in the former Austrian Embassy, said in a statement on Monday that Bridas is prepared to press ahead with the project while hostilities are still going on.
"In February 1996 we signed an agreement with the Government of the Islamic State of Afghanistan for the exclusive rights to build the pipeline," he said.

"This year, Bridas has visited all the different parties in Afghanistan and has confirmed the agreements with them to go forward with the pipeline project without waiting for the end of hostilities," he said.
Bridas is planning a pipeline of 1,306 km, including 135 km in Turkmenistan, 795 km in Afghanistan and 377 km in Pakistan.
The $2.5 billion project will have a throughput of 20 billion cubic metres a year through a 48 inch diameter line with an operating pressure of 95 bars, and there will be six compressor stations.

Last December, Mullah Sher Abbas Stanakzai, acting deputy foreign minister in Afghanistan's Taleban administration, told Reuters that Bridas was one of three contenders to build a pipeline on the route.
The others are a consortium of Unocal of the United States and Delta Oil of Saudi Arabia, and Daewoo of South Korea.
